detail.title: Investigating Mechanisms of Observer Disagreement and Predictive Calibration
detail.summary: This journal entry documents ongoing research into how independent observers—whether biological or artificial—reach divergent conclusions when analyzing identical data. By situating disagreement not as an error of perception but as a feature of divergent predictive priors and context-dependent calibration, we aim to map the structural limitations of consensus. We also continue our analysis of predictive processing in musical experience, leveraging current evidence to refine our model of how expectation-mismatch drives emotional valence. This research prioritizes the identification of falsifiable mechanisms that explain how persistent, honest disagreement can occur within rigorous frameworks.
